causes.filter-blockage: a blockage in the pump filter
causes.impeller-obstruction: something caught in the pump impeller
causes.hose-or-waste-restriction: a kink or blockage in the drain hose or waste pipe
causes.household-waste-backflow: a blockage in the household waste plumbing
causes.excess-suds: too much foam from the detergent
causes.control: the control circuit that drives the pump
causes.obstruction-beyond-reach: a blockage at the pump that can't be reached from the filter opening

checks.say: The most common cause is a blockage in the pump filter (also called the drain filter or trap), and it's a free fix. On most washing machines it's behind a small flap or kick-plate at the bottom front.
checks.ask: Could you check the filter and tell me what you find — was it clear, did you find and remove something, is there a blockage you can't shift, or does anything look broken?

checks.say: A noise like that while it tries to empty, together with the water not going, usually means something is caught in the pump filter or in the pump just behind it, so the pump filter is the first thing to check, and it's often a free fix. On most washing machines it's behind a small flap or kick-plate at the bottom front.
checks.ask: Could you check the filter and tell me what you find — was it clear, did you find and remove something, is there a blockage you can't shift, or does anything look broken?

checks.say: Next, run a drain or spin-only programme and listen near the bottom front of the machine while it tries to pump out.
checks.ask: Does the water pump away, and can you hear the pump humming or is it silent?

checks.say: Now that the blockage is cleared, let's test it: run a drain or spin-only programme.
checks.ask: Does the water pump away now?

checks.say: With the filter out, shine a torch into the filter opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller (the vanes) with a finger.
checks.ask: Does it turn freely, was anything caught in it, is it jammed, or do the vanes look broken?

checks.say: The next thing to check is the drain hose at the back: look for kinks or crushing, and check where it goes into the standpipe or sink waste.
checks.ask: Was the hose clear, did you find and clear a kink or blockage, or is there one you can't clear?

checks.say: That helps narrow it down.
checks.ask: When it tries to drain, can you hear the pump humming or buzzing, or is it silent?
Is there water left standing in the drum?
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

checks.say: The simple checks are done, and what's left depends on your exact machine.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening, on the inside of the door or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.

causes.suspension-or-movement: the suspension (shock absorbers / springs) or the machine not standing level
causes.motor-brushes: worn carbon brushes in the motor
causes.motor-drive: the motor, its control or the speed sensing
causes.mechanical-resistance: the drum bearings or something jammed between the drum and tub

checks.say: First, let's rule out a drainage problem — a washing machine won't spin while water is still in it.
checks.ask: When it stops, is there water left standing in the drum (not just wet washing)?
During the wash part of the cycle, does the drum turn back and forth, or does it not turn at all?

checks.say: Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty.
checks.ask: Does it spin up properly when it's empty?

checks.say: Washing machines refuse to spin if the load is out of balance — a single heavy item such as a bath mat, rug, duvet or a pair of jeans on its own, or a very small load, is the usual trigger. Spreading the washing out evenly or adding a few smaller items usually lets it spin.
checks.ask: Was it a single heavy item or a very small load, or a normal mixed load?

checks.say: Next, run a spin-only (or rinse and spin) programme with the washing in.
checks.ask: Does the drum spin up properly on that programme?

checks.say: If you haven't already, change that (switch the option off, or even out the load), then run a rinse and spin or spin-only programme to test it.
checks.ask: Does it spin up properly now?

checks.say: It's also worth checking the settings: wool, delicate and hand-wash programmes spin very gently, and options such as "no spin", "rinse hold" or a low spin speed stop the final spin.
checks.ask: Was a normal programme with a normal spin speed selected, or was one of those options set?

checks.say: Next, check how the drum moves by hand.
checks.ask: With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?

checks.say: One more thing to listen for.
checks.ask: When it should be turning the drum, can you hear the motor running or humming, or is there no motor sound at all?

checks.say: A washing machine won't run if the door lock doesn't engage. Close the door firmly, check nothing like a sock or the seal is caught in it, and start a programme.
checks.ask: Does the door click locked and the lock light come on?

checks.say: What's left depends on how your machine is built (belt or direct drive, brushed or brushless motor).
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening, on the inside of the door or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

causes.oversudsing: too much (or the wrong) detergent foaming over
causes.filter-seal: the pump filter cap or its seal
causes.inlet-connection: the fill hose or its tap connection
causes.inlet-valve-or-fill: the fill side inside the machine (inlet valve or its hoses)
causes.drain-connection: the drain hose or its standpipe connection
causes.tub-or-major-internal: the drum tub or another internal part

checks.say: Let's pin down where the water is coming from.
checks.ask: Where do you see it first — around the door, from the detergent drawer, at the back where the hoses are, at the pump filter flap at the bottom front, or just a puddle underneath?

checks.say: Next, when it happens tells us a lot.
checks.ask: Does it leak while it's filling, during the wash, while it drains or spins, or even when the machine is off?

checks.say: Front leaks are most often the rubber door seal. Open the door and look all the way round the seal, including inside the folds at the bottom — a trapped coin, underwire or sock can hold it open, and splits often hide in the folds.
checks.ask: Is the seal intact, did you find something trapped in it, or is it torn or split?

checks.say: Pull the detergent drawer out (most have a release tab) and rinse away any built-up powder or softener, and check the housing it slides into for gunk.
checks.ask: Was it blocked or built up, already clean, or cracked or broken?

checks.say: Too much detergent, or one that isn't low-foam (HE), can foam over and push water out.
checks.ask: How much detergent do you use, and is it a low-foam (HE) washing-machine detergent?

checks.say: The pump filter cap at the bottom front is a common leak, especially if it's been opened recently. Check it's screwed in fully and straight, and that its rubber seal is clean.
checks.ask: Was it loose or not seated, tight and dry already, or is the cap or seal cracked or damaged?

checks.say: Check the fill hose where it screws onto the tap and onto the back of the machine — a loose fitting or a missing or perished washer is the usual cause.
checks.ask: Were the connections loose (and are they tight now), already tight and dry, or is the hose split or bulging?

checks.say: Check the grey drain hose along its length and where it goes into the standpipe or sink waste.
checks.ask: Was it loose or pushed in too far, sound and dry, or is the hose split or cracked?

checks.say: Now run a short programme and keep an eye on the floor.
checks.ask: Does it stay dry, or does it still leak?

checks.say: Now run a short programme and keep an eye on the floor.
checks.ask: Does it stay dry, or does it still leak?

checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening, on the inside of the door or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

causes.tap-or-fill-hose: the tap or the fill hose
causes.door-interlock: the door lock (the machine won't fill until the door locks)
causes.pressure-or-control: the water-level sensing or the control side

checks.say: Let's narrow down the fill problem.
checks.ask: When it starts, does no water come in at all, or does it come in but only very slowly?

checks.say: First, the supply to the house.
checks.ask: Do your other taps (for example the kitchen cold tap) run at normal pressure right now?

checks.say: Most machines won't let any water in until the door has locked.
checks.ask: When you start a programme, does the door click locked (and the lock light come on)?

checks.say: Open the door, make sure nothing is caught in the seal, then close it firmly until it clicks and start a programme.
checks.ask: Does the door click locked now?

checks.say: Check the tap the fill hose connects to is turned fully on, and that the hose behind the machine isn't kinked or squashed against the wall.
checks.ask: Was the tap fully on and the hose clear, did you find it off or kinked (and sort it), or is the hose itself damaged?

checks.say: Where the fill hose screws onto the back of the machine there's a small mesh filter that can block with grit or scale. Unscrew the hose at the machine end and look into the inlet.
checks.ask: Was the mesh blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

checks.say: Now turn the tap back on and start a programme.
checks.ask: Does it fill normally now, or is it still not taking water?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.household-supply: If your other taps are weak or off too, the problem is the household water supply rather than the machine. Check the stopcock and whether your water supplier has reported an outage or low pressure; a plumber can help if it's a house problem. No machine part is needed.
conclusionNotes.F7:tap-or-fill-hose: The tap or a kinked hose was very likely stopping the water, so no part is needed. Keep the hose free of kinks when you push the machine back.

causes.foam-level: too much detergent foam upsetting the level sensing
causes.waste-backflow: waste water backing up from the household plumbing
causes.level-sensing-or-control: the water-level sensing or the control side

checks.say: This tells us which part is letting the water in.
checks.ask: When the machine is switched off at the socket, does water still keep running in (into the drawer or the drum)?

checks.say: With the machine switched off at the socket, turn the tap back on and watch the detergent drawer and the drum for a minute.
checks.ask: Did any water run in while the machine was switched off?

checks.say: The kind of water tells us where it's coming from.
checks.ask: Is the water that appears clean like tap water, or dirty and smelly like waste water?

checks.say: Next, how high the water actually gets.
checks.ask: While it's running, does the water rise above the bottom of the door glass, or does it keep taking water while the level looks normal?

checks.say: Check how the grey drain hose is fitted at the back: it should rise high (hooked near the top of the machine or the standpipe) and go no more than a hand's width down the standpipe or sink waste. If it hangs low or is pushed far in, water can siphon away as it fills.
checks.ask: Was it low or pushed in too far (and have you refitted it), or was it already fitted correctly?

checks.say: Turn the tap back on and start a short programme.
checks.ask: Does it fill to a normal level and stop now, or does it still keep taking water?

checks.say: To match the right valve for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.O7:drain-hose-siphon: The drain hose fitting was very likely letting the water siphon away (so it kept refilling), so no part is needed. Keep the hose hooked up high.
conclusionNotes.drain-hose-siphon: This points to the drain hose installation: if it sits too low or too far down the waste, water siphons out as it fills (or dirty water runs back in). Refitting it high is an installation fix, not a part — a plumber or installer can sort it if needed.

causes.normal-release-delay: the normal safety delay before the door unlocks
causes.level-sensing-or-control: the water-level sensing or the control side (it thinks there is still water in)

checks.say: Let's pin down what the door is doing.
checks.ask: Does the door not open, not lock when you start a programme, not close properly, is the handle broken, or does the lock keep clicking on and off?

checks.say: The door stays locked on purpose while there's water inside.
checks.ask: Can you see any water left in the drum through the glass?

checks.say: Doors often stay locked for a couple of minutes after a programme ends. Leave it switched on for 5 minutes and try the handle normally. If it's still locked, switch it off at the socket, wait another 5 minutes and try again.
checks.ask: Does the door open now?

checks.say: Many machines have a child lock (often a key or padlock symbol, turned off by holding two buttons together for a few seconds — your manual shows which) that keeps the door and buttons locked.
checks.ask: Was the child lock on (and is it off now), or was it already off?

checks.say: Open the door, make sure nothing is caught in the seal, then close it firmly until it clicks and start a programme.
checks.ask: Does the door click locked now?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged, look at the small hook (catch) on the door and the slot it goes into, and check the door lines up squarely when you close it.
checks.ask: Is the catch broken, bent or the door dropped on its hinge, was something blocking it (now cleared), or does it all look fine?

checks.say: Now close the door and start a programme.
checks.ask: Is the door working normally now, or does the problem still happen?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.D7:child-lock: The child lock was very likely holding it, so no part is needed.
conclusionNotes.door-lock: This points to the door lock (interlock) or its release. Please don't force it or try to bypass it; an appliance engineer can confirm it safely — I'm not recommending a part from this.

causes.transit-bolts: the transit bolts still being fitted
causes.load-imbalance: the load being out of balance

checks.say: A new or recently moved machine is the most common reason for violent shaking.
checks.ask: Was the machine recently installed, delivered or moved?

checks.say: New machines come with transit (shipping) bolts in the back panel that lock the drum for delivery — usually three or four large bolts with plastic spacers. If they're still in, the drum can't move freely and the whole machine shakes.
checks.ask: Are any transit bolts still fitted (and have you taken them out), or were they already removed?

checks.say: A single heavy item (a bath mat, rug, duvet or pair of jeans) or a very small load can throw the drum off balance.
checks.ask: Was it one heavy item or a small load (and have you evened it out), or a normal mixed load?

checks.say: Check it stands level and firm: press on each top corner — it shouldn't rock — and make sure all four feet touch a solid floor with their lock nuts tight.
checks.ask: Did it rock or was a foot loose (and have you adjusted it), or was it already level and firm?

checks.say: Take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty.
checks.ask: Does it still shake or bang violently with the drum empty, or is it smooth?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side.
checks.ask: Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?

checks.say: Now run a normal load with a spin.
checks.ask: Is it spinning smoothly now, or does it still shake badly?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.V7:transit-bolts: The transit bolts were very likely the cause, so no part is needed. Keep them in case you move the machine again.
conclusionNotes.V7:levelling-or-floor: Levelling it was very likely the fix, so no part is needed. Re-check the feet now and then — they can work loose.
conclusionNotes.V7:load-imbalance: That was the load being out of balance, so no part is needed. Wash heavy items with a few towels to even them out.
conclusionNotes.transit-bolts: If the machine was recently installed, transit bolts still being fitted would explain this — please check the back panel before anything else. No part is needed for that.
conclusionNotes.levelling-or-floor: This points to how the machine stands: it needs to be level, with all four feet locked, on a solid floor (suspended wooden floors can bounce). That's an installation fix rather than a part.
conclusionNotes.drum-support-or-bearings: A loose or rumbling drum points to the drum support or bearings. Please stop using it on fast spins and have an appliance engineer check it — I'm not recommending a part from this.

causes.pump-obstruction: something caught in the drain pump
causes.foreign-object: an object loose in the drum or between the drum and tub
causes.load-or-installation: the load or how the machine is installed
causes.belt-pulley-or-motor: the drive belt, pulley or motor

checks.say: When the noise happens tells us a lot.
checks.ask: Do you hear it while it fills, during the wash, while it drains, on the spin, or all the time?

checks.say: Next, what it sounds like.
checks.ask: Is it more of a grinding or rumbling, a hum, a metallic scraping, a knock or bang, a rattle, a squeal, or a click?

checks.say: A new or recently moved machine can knock if it wasn't set up fully.
checks.ask: Was the machine recently installed, delivered or moved?

checks.say: A noise while draining is often a coin, button or hair grip caught at the pump. Open the small flap at the bottom front and slowly unscrew the pump filter.
checks.ask: Did you find anything caught in the filter (and clear it), or was it clear?

checks.say: With the filter still out, shine a torch into the opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller with a finger.
checks.ask: Does it turn freely with nothing caught, did you find and clear something, or is it broken or rough?

checks.say: Look all round the inside of the drum, under the paddles and in the folds of the door seal for a coin, bra wire or other object. Turn the drum slowly by hand and listen for anything sliding or catching.
checks.ask: Did you find something and remove it, can you see or hear something stuck that you can't get out, or is there nothing there?

checks.say: New machines come with transit (shipping) bolts in the back panel that lock the drum for delivery. If they're still in, it bangs on the spin.
checks.ask: Are any transit bolts still fitted (and have you taken them out), or were they already removed?

checks.say: A single heavy item or a very small load can knock and bang as it spins.
checks.ask: Was it one heavy item or a small load (and have you evened it out), or a normal mixed load?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged, turn the drum slowly by hand a few times and listen.
checks.ask: Does it turn smoothly and quietly, or does it feel rough or grind as it turns?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side.
checks.ask: Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?

checks.say: Now run a normal programme again.
checks.ask: Has the noise gone, or can you still hear it?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.

conclusionNotes.N7:load-or-installation: That was the load or the set-up rather than a fault, so no part is needed.

causes.fill-or-level: the water level (the heater only runs once it has filled)

checks.say: Modern machines often wash cool on purpose — eco, quick and 20–30°C programmes barely heat, and the door glass can stay cool even when the water is warm.
checks.ask: Which programme and temperature were you using — a 40°C or hotter cottons wash, or an eco, quick or low-temperature one?

checks.say: To check properly, run a 60°C cottons programme (not eco or quick) with a normal load, and take the washing out as soon as it finishes.
checks.ask: Does the washing come out warm, or still cold?

checks.say: One more thing that helps.
checks.ask: Does the programme take much longer than usual, or seem to get stuck part way through?

checks.say: Now run a 60°C cottons wash again.
checks.ask: Does the washing come out warm now, or still cold?

checks.say: A washer-dryer heats in two places — the wash water and the drying air — and they use different heaters.
checks.ask: Is it the wash water that stays cold, or does it not heat when it's drying?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.H7:programme-setting: The temperature setting was very likely the reason, so no part is needed.
conclusionNotes.temperature-sensor: This points to the temperature sensor or its wiring. That needs an appliance engineer to test safely — I'm not recommending a part from this.
conclusionNotes.heating-control: The heating control or wiring is the most likely area. That needs an appliance engineer to test safely — I'm not recommending a part from this.
conclusionNotes.fill-or-level: The heater only switches on once the machine has filled to the right level, so a fill or level problem can stop it heating. An appliance engineer is the best next step — I'm not recommending a part from this.

causes.foam-or-wrong-detergent: foam from washing-up liquid or the wrong detergent
causes.loading-or-spray-escape: spray being deflected out of the door by the loading
causes.internal-leak: a leak inside the dishwasher (sump, pump seal or an internal hose)

checks.say: Let's pin down where the water is coming from.
checks.ask: Do you see it first at the door, at the back where the hoses are, or underneath the dishwasher?

checks.say: When it leaks tells us a lot.
checks.ask: Does it leak while it's filling, during the wash, while it drains, or even when it's switched off?

checks.say: Washing-up liquid — even a little left on rinsed dishes — makes masses of foam that pushes out past the door.
checks.ask: Could any washing-up liquid or hand-wash liquid have got into the dishwasher, or do you only use dishwasher tablets / detergent?

checks.say: Open the door and look all the way round the rubber seal on the tub edge, and along the bottom of the door, for splits, flattened sections or something caught on it.
checks.ask: Is the seal damaged, was something caught on it (now removed), or does it look fine?

checks.say: Tall trays or items hanging below the lower rack can deflect the spray straight at the door seal. With the racks loaded, turn each spray arm by hand.
checks.ask: Was anything catching the arms or pointing at the door (and have you moved it), or is everything clear?

checks.say: Dishwashers have a base tray with a flood-protection float: if water collects there, it stops filling and often keeps pumping on purpose.
checks.ask: Looking under the front kick plate, can you see water in the base tray, or a flood / tap warning on the display?

checks.say: Check where the inlet hose connects at the tap under the sink and at the dishwasher end for drips, a loose fitting or a split.
checks.ask: Was a connection loose (and is it tight now), is the hose damaged, or is it dry?

checks.say: Check the drain hose along its length and where it joins the sink waste for drips, a loose clip or a split.
checks.ask: Was it loose (and is it refitted now), is the hose split, or is it dry?

checks.say: Now run a short programme and keep an eye on the floor.
checks.ask: Does it stay dry, or does it still leak?

checks.say: To match the right part for your dishwasher I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate along the edge of the door or the side of the tub — a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a dishwasher, a washing machine or a washer-dryer?

conclusionNotes.foam-or-wrong-detergent: Washing-up liquid makes far more foam than a dishwasher can hold, and it pushes water out past the door. Mop up, run a rinse (or two) with the door shut and nothing added, and only use dishwasher detergent — no part is needed.
conclusionNotes.K7:loading-or-spray-escape: That was the spray being deflected out of the door, so no part is needed. Keep tall items clear of the spray arms.

causes.pump-obstruction: something caught at the drain pump
causes.drain-hose-restriction: a kinked or blocked drain hose

checks.say: Let's check what's left after the programme.
checks.ask: Is there still dirty water sitting in the bottom of the tub (inside, under the lower rack)?

checks.say: Take out the lower rack, then twist and lift out the filter in the bottom of the tub. Rinse it under the tap and clear any food, grease or glass from the sump underneath.
checks.ask: Was the filter or sump blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

checks.say: With the filter out, bail out any water with a cup and sponge. There's a small pump cover in the sump — lift its clip and look underneath with a torch for glass, stones or bones, then gently turn the little impeller with a finger.
checks.ask: Did you find something caught (and remove it), is the impeller broken, or does it turn freely with nothing there?

checks.say: Check the grey drain hose from the back of the dishwasher to the sink waste isn't kinked or squashed — especially where it runs behind the plinth or under the sink.
checks.ask: Was the hose kinked or blocked (and is it clear now), or is it running freely?

checks.say: Under the sink, look where the drain hose joins the waste. On a newly fitted sink waste the little blanking plug inside the spigot has to be cut out, and the sink trap mustn't be blocked — run the sink tap and check it drains freely.
checks.ask: Was the blanking plug still in or the trap blocked (and is it cleared now), or is the connection fine?

checks.say: With the filter back in, close the door, choose cancel or a drain / rinse programme and let it run for a couple of minutes, listening near the bottom of the machine.
checks.ask: Did the water pump away this time?

checks.say: One more thing that helps.
checks.ask: While it tried to drain, could you hear the pump humming or running, or was it silent?

checks.say: Now run a normal programme again and see whether the problem comes back.
checks.ask: Is it working normally now, or does the problem still happen?

checks.say: To match the right part for your dishwasher I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate along the edge of the door or the side of the tub — a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a dishwasher, a washing machine or a washer-dryer?

conclusionNotes.household-waste-or-spigot: If the sink or waste backs up when the dishwasher drains, the blockage is in the household waste (the sink trap, waste pipe or spigot), not the dishwasher. Clearing that, or a plumber, is the next step — no dishwasher part is needed.
conclusionNotes.A7:household-waste-or-spigot: The sink waste connection was very likely the cause, so no dishwasher part is needed.

causes.tap-hose-or-aquastop: the tap, inlet hose or its AquaStop safety valve
causes.door-not-recognised: the door latch / switch (it won't fill until the door is recognised as shut)
causes.fill-sensing-or-control: the fill sensing or the control side

checks.say: Let's narrow down the fill problem.
checks.ask: After it starts, does no water come in at all, or only a little?

checks.say: First, the supply to the house.
checks.ask: Do your other taps (for example the kitchen cold tap) run at normal pressure right now?

checks.say: Many dishwashers have a flood-protection float in the base: if any water collects there, they stop filling (and often keep pumping) on purpose.
checks.ask: Can you see any water in the base under the front kick plate, or a flood / tap warning symbol on the display?

checks.say: It won't let water in until it knows the door is shut.
checks.ask: When you close the door and press start, does it show the door is open (or a door light stay on)?

checks.say: Open the door, make sure nothing in the racks is sticking out, then shut it firmly until it clicks and press start.
checks.ask: Does it still show the door as open?

checks.ask: Does it stay dry, or does it still leak?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening, on the inside of the door or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.

causes.tap-or-fill-hose: the tap or the fill hose
causes.door-interlock: the door lock (the machine won't fill until the door locks)
causes.pressure-or-control: the water-level sensing or the control side

checks.say: Let's narrow down the fill problem.
checks.ask: When it starts, does no water come in at all, or does it come in but only very slowly?

checks.say: First, the supply to the house.
checks.ask: Do your other taps (for example the kitchen cold tap) run at normal pressure right now?

checks.say: Most machines won't let any water in until the door has locked.
checks.ask: When you start a programme, does the door click locked (and the lock light come on)?

checks.say: Open the door, make sure nothing is caught in the seal, then close it firmly until it clicks and start a programme.
checks.ask: Does the door click locked now?

checks.say: Check the tap the fill hose connects to is turned fully on, and that the hose behind the machine isn't kinked or squashed against the wall.
checks.ask: Was the tap fully on and the hose clear, did you find it off or kinked (and sort it), or is the hose itself damaged?

checks.say: Where the fill hose screws onto the back of the machine there's a small mesh filter that can block with grit or scale. Unscrew the hose at the machine end and look into the inlet.
checks.ask: Was the mesh blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?

checks.say: Now turn the tap back on and start a programme.
checks.ask: Does it fill normally now, or is it still not taking water?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.household-supply: If your other taps are weak or off too, the problem is the household water supply rather than the machine. Check the stopcock and whether your water supplier has reported an outage or low pressure; a plumber can help if it's a house problem. No machine part is needed.
conclusionNotes.F7:tap-or-fill-hose: The tap or a kinked hose was very likely stopping the water, so no part is needed. Keep the hose free of kinks when you push the machine back.

causes.foam-level: too much detergent foam upsetting the level sensing
causes.waste-backflow: waste water backing up from the household plumbing
causes.level-sensing-or-control: the water-level sensing or the control side

checks.say: This tells us which part is letting the water in.
checks.ask: When the machine is switched off at the socket, does water still keep running in (into the drawer or the drum)?

checks.say: With the machine switched off at the socket, turn the tap back on and watch the detergent drawer and the drum for a minute.
checks.ask: Did any water run in while the machine was switched off?

checks.say: The kind of water tells us where it's coming from.
checks.ask: Is the water that appears clean like tap water, or dirty and smelly like waste water?

checks.say: Next, how high the water actually gets.
checks.ask: While it's running, does the water rise above the bottom of the door glass, or does it keep taking water while the level looks normal?

checks.say: Check how the grey drain hose is fitted at the back: it should rise high (hooked near the top of the machine or the standpipe) and go no more than a hand's width down the standpipe or sink waste. If it hangs low or is pushed far in, water can siphon away as it fills.
checks.ask: Was it low or pushed in too far (and have you refitted it), or was it already fitted correctly?

checks.say: Turn the tap back on and start a short programme.
checks.ask: Does it fill to a normal level and stop now, or does it still keep taking water?

checks.say: To match the right valve for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.O7:drain-hose-siphon: The drain hose fitting was very likely letting the water siphon away (so it kept refilling), so no part is needed. Keep the hose hooked up high.
conclusionNotes.drain-hose-siphon: This points to the drain hose installation: if it sits too low or too far down the waste, water siphons out as it fills (or dirty water runs back in). Refitting it high is an installation fix, not a part — a plumber or installer can sort it if needed.

causes.normal-release-delay: the normal safety delay before the door unlocks
causes.level-sensing-or-control: the water-level sensing or the control side (it thinks there is still water in)

checks.say: Let's pin down what the door is doing.
checks.ask: Does the door not open, not lock when you start a programme, not close properly, is the handle broken, or does the lock keep clicking on and off?

checks.say: The door stays locked on purpose while there's water inside.
checks.ask: Can you see any water left in the drum through the glass?

checks.say: Doors often stay locked for a couple of minutes after a programme ends. Leave it switched on for 5 minutes and try the handle normally. If it's still locked, switch it off at the socket, wait another 5 minutes and try again.
checks.ask: Does the door open now?

checks.say: Many machines have a child lock (often a key or padlock symbol, turned off by holding two buttons together for a few seconds — your manual shows which) that keeps the door and buttons locked.
checks.ask: Was the child lock on (and is it off now), or was it already off?

checks.say: Open the door, make sure nothing is caught in the seal, then close it firmly until it clicks and start a programme.
checks.ask: Does the door click locked now?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged, look at the small hook (catch) on the door and the slot it goes into, and check the door lines up squarely when you close it.
checks.ask: Is the catch broken, bent or the door dropped on its hinge, was something blocking it (now cleared), or does it all look fine?

checks.say: Now close the door and start a programme.
checks.ask: Is the door working normally now, or does the problem still happen?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.D7:child-lock: The child lock was very likely holding it, so no part is needed.
conclusionNotes.door-lock: This points to the door lock (interlock) or its release. Please don't force it or try to bypass it; an appliance engineer can confirm it safely — I'm not recommending a part from this.

causes.transit-bolts: the transit bolts still being fitted
causes.load-imbalance: the load being out of balance

checks.say: A new or recently moved machine is the most common reason for violent shaking.
checks.ask: Was the machine recently installed, delivered or moved?

checks.say: New machines come with transit (shipping) bolts in the back panel that lock the drum for delivery — usually three or four large bolts with plastic spacers. If they're still in, the drum can't move freely and the whole machine shakes.
checks.ask: Are any transit bolts still fitted (and have you taken them out), or were they already removed?

checks.say: A single heavy item (a bath mat, rug, duvet or pair of jeans) or a very small load can throw the drum off balance.
checks.ask: Was it one heavy item or a small load (and have you evened it out), or a normal mixed load?

checks.say: Check it stands level and firm: press on each top corner — it shouldn't rock — and make sure all four feet touch a solid floor with their lock nuts tight.
checks.ask: Did it rock or was a foot loose (and have you adjusted it), or was it already level and firm?

checks.say: Take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty.
checks.ask: Does it still shake or bang violently with the drum empty, or is it smooth?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side.
checks.ask: Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?

checks.say: Now run a normal load with a spin.
checks.ask: Is it spinning smoothly now, or does it still shake badly?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.V7:transit-bolts: The transit bolts were very likely the cause, so no part is needed. Keep them in case you move the machine again.
conclusionNotes.V7:levelling-or-floor: Levelling it was very likely the fix, so no part is needed. Re-check the feet now and then — they can work loose.
conclusionNotes.V7:load-imbalance: That was the load being out of balance, so no part is needed. Wash heavy items with a few towels to even them out.
conclusionNotes.transit-bolts: If the machine was recently installed, transit bolts still being fitted would explain this — please check the back panel before anything else. No part is needed for that.
conclusionNotes.levelling-or-floor: This points to how the machine stands: it needs to be level, with all four feet locked, on a solid floor (suspended wooden floors can bounce). That's an installation fix rather than a part.
conclusionNotes.drum-support-or-bearings: A loose or rumbling drum points to the drum support or bearings. Please stop using it on fast spins and have an appliance engineer check it — I'm not recommending a part from this.

causes.pump-obstruction: something caught in the drain pump
causes.foreign-object: an object loose in the drum or between the drum and tub
causes.load-or-installation: the load or how the machine is installed
causes.belt-pulley-or-motor: the drive belt, pulley or motor

checks.say: When the noise happens tells us a lot.
checks.ask: Do you hear it while it fills, during the wash, while it drains, on the spin, or all the time?

checks.say: Next, what it sounds like.
checks.ask: Is it more of a grinding or rumbling, a hum, a metallic scraping, a knock or bang, a rattle, a squeal, or a click?

checks.say: A new or recently moved machine can knock if it wasn't set up fully.
checks.ask: Was the machine recently installed, delivered or moved?

checks.say: A noise while draining is often a coin, button or hair grip caught at the pump. Open the small flap at the bottom front and slowly unscrew the pump filter.
checks.ask: Did you find anything caught in the filter (and clear it), or was it clear?

checks.say: With the filter still out, shine a torch into the opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller with a finger.
checks.ask: Does it turn freely with nothing caught, did you find and clear something, or is it broken or rough?

checks.say: Look all round the inside of the drum, under the paddles and in the folds of the door seal for a coin, bra wire or other object. Turn the drum slowly by hand and listen for anything sliding or catching.
checks.ask: Did you find something and remove it, can you see or hear something stuck that you can't get out, or is there nothing there?

checks.say: New machines come with transit (shipping) bolts in the back panel that lock the drum for delivery. If they're still in, it bangs on the spin.
checks.ask: Are any transit bolts still fitted (and have you taken them out), or were they already removed?

checks.say: A single heavy item or a very small load can knock and bang as it spins.
checks.ask: Was it one heavy item or a small load (and have you evened it out), or a normal mixed load?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged, turn the drum slowly by hand a few times and listen.
checks.ask: Does it turn smoothly and quietly, or does it feel rough or grind as it turns?

checks.say: With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side.
checks.ask: Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?

checks.say: Now run a normal programme again.
checks.ask: Has the noise gone, or can you still hear it?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.N7:load-or-installation: That was the load or the set-up rather than a fault, so no part is needed.

causes.fill-or-level: the water level (the heater only runs once it has filled)

checks.say: Modern machines often wash cool on purpose — eco, quick and 20–30°C programmes barely heat, and the door glass can stay cool even when the water is warm.
checks.ask: Which programme and temperature were you using — a 40°C or hotter cottons wash, or an eco, quick or low-temperature one?

checks.say: To check properly, run a 60°C cottons programme (not eco or quick) with a normal load, and take the washing out as soon as it finishes.
checks.ask: Does the washing come out warm, or still cold?

checks.say: One more thing that helps.
checks.ask: Does the programme take much longer than usual, or seem to get stuck part way through?

checks.say: Now run a 60°C cottons wash again.
checks.ask: Does the washing come out warm now, or still cold?

checks.say: A washer-dryer heats in two places — the wash water and the drying air — and they use different heaters.
checks.ask: Is it the wash water that stays cold, or does it not heat when it's drying?

checks.say: To match the right part for your machine I need its exact model.
checks.ask: Could you send me the model number? It's on the rating plate — usually around the door opening or on the back — and a photo of the label is fine.
Is it a washing machine, a washer-dryer or a dishwasher?

conclusionNotes.H7:programme-setting: The temperature setting was very likely the reason, so no part is needed.
conclusionNotes.temperature-sensor: This points to the temperature sensor or its wiring. That needs an appliance engineer to test safely — I'm not recommending a part from this.
conclusionNotes.heating-control: The heating control or wiring is the most likely area. That needs an appliance engineer to test safely — I'm not recommending a part from this.
conclusionNotes.fill-or-level: The heater only switches on once the machine has filled to the right level, so a fill or level problem can stop it heating. An appliance engineer is the best next step — I'm not recommending a part from this.
